title: His other pieces: Chow Chow, Dixie Queen, Fans and Glances
summary: Interviewer asks about Hoffman's compositions; she describes the delicate character of his pieces.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yes. What about something like Chow Chow? Do you remember that piece he wrote?
Dixie. I probably knew of it at the time.
But it didn't mean anything to me.
And you've got Dixie Queen. Did that make much of a hit?
I don't know. I don't think. I don't know.
Or Fans and Glances is another one I discovered in that article.

Well, Fans and Glances comes under a little bit, and that voluptuous come under a different, you'd have to be a pianist or something like that. It would never be used at a dance or among young people. But he had that kind of a delicate idea to his pieces, his music and things, besides the ring time.
Yeah. I noticed one of them was Coquette Waltz.
